$note: Single source of truth for the three style mockups. Colours are hex so SwiftUI (Color) and Jetpack Compose (Color) can read them directly. build.py turns each style into CSS variables.

shared.stateRule: Protection state is always shown with an icon and words, never colour alone.

toi-gian.label: Tối giản

font.web: -apple-system, 'SF Pro Text', system-ui, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif

toi-gian.depth: Hairlines only. No shadows, no blur.

motion.character: Fades and short slides. Nothing bounces.

platform.shared: Everything. System font, flat surfaces and hairlines exist on both platforms.
platform.iosOnly: On iOS 26 the sheet and toolbar pick up system Liquid Glass automatically.
platform.android: Use Material 3 bottom sheet with tonal elevation set to 0.

tuong-phan-cao.label: Tương phản cao

font.web: -apple-system, 'SF Pro Text', system-ui, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif
font.ios: SF Pro bold + SF Mono labels

tuong-phan-cao.depth: 2px solid outlines. No shadows, no transparency.

motion.character: Near-instant. State changes are shown by shape and words.

platform.shared: Everything. Contrast is 21:1 for body text and about 15:1 for yellow on black.
platform.iosOnly: Honour Increase Contrast and Bold Text. Opt custom surfaces out of Liquid Glass.
platform.android: Honour font scale and high-contrast text. Disable dynamic colour so the yellow stays fixed.

vi-tuong-tac.label: Vi tương tác
vi-tuong-tac.depth: Soft shadows tinted with the accent. One level only.

motion.character: Springs with a little overshoot. Every tap answers back: press squish, shield pulse, stamp and confetti on block, swipe to unblock.

platform.shared: Durations, spring values, colours and the sequence of each interaction.
platform.iosOnly: Haptics via sensoryFeedback (iOS 17+) or UIImpactFeedbackGenerator on iOS 16. SF Pro Rounded is built in.
platform.android: Haptics via HapticFeedback; strength varies by device. A rounded font must be bundled. Compose spring() takes stiffness and dampingRatio, so convert the spring values.
